# Markdown Viewer

Full-stack markdown editor with LLM-powered transformations (OpenRouter), GitHub and BookStack
integrations, and multi-format export via pandoc. The defining characteristic: a vanilla-JS
frontend with **no build step** and a Flask REST backend that ship twice from one codebase —
on the web (Docker + nginx) and inside an Electron desktop wrapper (`app://` protocol,
PyInstaller backend).

> Status: **implemented and in use** — v2.7.2; web and desktop builds are shipped; backend,
> frontend and desktop each have a test suite with an 80% coverage gate.
> [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) is the authoritative design source; `docs/chats/` holds
> prior conversation context.
>
> Build & test: `source venv/bin/activate && cd backend && pytest`, `npm test -- --run`,
> `npm run test:e2e`, `cd desktop && npm test`.

## Read before making changes

1. [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) — system structure, components, stability zones.
2. The relevant `AI_*.md` file(s) for the code you are touching — coding rules (see below).
3. `docs/chats/` and the root/doc `*.md` files — previous talks and implementations on similar
   tasks; check them before proposing anything.

Follow all applicable `AI_*.md` files strictly; do not redefine or duplicate them.
`ARCHITECTURE.md` and the `AI_*.md` files must not redefine or duplicate each other's content.

## Working agreement

- **Confirm before acting.** Never create, edit, or delete files, run state-changing commands,
  or write to external systems without explicit user approval. First explain the situation,
  propose specifics (which files, what changes, what commands), then wait for a clear "yes."
  Read-only work (reading, searching, analyzing, answering) needs no confirmation.
  Exception: if the user says "just do it" / "go ahead," proceed directly. This includes the
  project rule: **never start writing code right after a user question** — propose the
  solution and wait for an explicit request to implement.
- **Don't commit unprompted.** Never stage and commit — only the user does this. Run
  `git add` / `git commit` / `git push` only when the user explicitly asks — never as an
  unrequested side-effect of another task.
- **Never weaken a gate or fake a mock to make a check pass.** The 80% coverage gates
  (`--cov-fail-under=80` in `backend/pytest.ini`, the thresholds in `vitest.config.js`) and the
  external-API mocks are the honest signal; tests must never make real paid OpenRouter calls
  and must not replace a failing assertion with a looser one. Surface the honest failure
  instead.
- **Verify against the wrapped APIs, don't assume.** OpenRouter, GitHub REST v3, BookStack and
  the pandoc CLI are external contracts: before designing or changing anything that touches
  them (transform payloads, OAuth flows, page CRUD, export flags), check the real behavior —
  the installed client sources (`source venv/bin/activate && pip show -f openrouter`),
  `docs/BOOKSTACK_API_INTEGRATION.md`, `pandoc --help` — not memory or inference. Cite the
  file you verified against so the claim is checkable.
- **Verify against this codebase — don't describe it from memory.** Every factual claim about
  how _this project_ behaves — a file path, which fields a component renders, when a code path
  actually runs, a payload or API shape, a config key — must be read out of the source before
  it is stated. This applies to **prose as much as to code**: answers, design docs, test
  plans, and manual steps handed to the user. Prose is where the errors concentrate, because
  `pytest`, `npm test` and `cd desktop && npm test` catch a wrong edit but never catch a wrong
  sentence. Recurring traps: dev ports are 8000 (frontend) / 5050 (backend) / dynamic
  (desktop); packaged Electron resources land directly in `Contents/Resources/`, not an
  `app-resources/` subdirectory; PyInstaller hidden imports must be `backend.*`-prefixed only;
  `npm run make` can exit 0 without producing an installer. Search with the `semantic-index`
  skill first (`.index/` exists; re-index when stale), then fall back to Grep/Glob/Read once
  the symbol or filename is known. Cite `file:line` so the claim is checkable. Having built
  the thing in this same session is **not** verification — that memory is exactly what drifts.
- **Document architecture as-is, not as imagined.**
- **Stop and ask** if anything is unclear or contradictory.

## Tooling

- **Backend:** Python 3.11+ / Flask 3.0; root `venv/` — `source venv/bin/activate` for all
  backend tests and application runs. No linter/mypy gate exists; PEP8 + type hints by
  convention (AI_FLASK.md).
- **Frontend:** vanilla ES6 modules, no build step, no TypeScript, no ESLint/Prettier;
  Vitest + happy-dom + MSW for units (80% thresholds enforced), Playwright for E2E (web
  servers auto-started by `playwright.config.js`).
- **Desktop:** Electron 33+ / Forge 7 / CommonJS (`desktop/` has its own `package.json` and
  `node_modules`; `electron-store` v7 and `get-port` pinned for CJS); Vitest unit tests;
  `npm run make` builds the DMG — verify `desktop/out/make/` was actually updated.
- **Secrets:** `.env` (gitignored) with `.env.example` committed; on desktop,
  `electron-store` replaces `.env`.
- No CI pipeline, no database/ORM, no bundler are part of this project — don't assume their
  presence.
